resolution: Built the Studio 'detach' op the user specified for car panels (hood/door/trunk/lights): select a face-group on the body, click detach, and it peels off into its own thin solid part. Three pure+headless editMesh functions — subMeshFromFaces (extract a face-group into a compact standalone mesh), solidifyFaces (outer skin + per-vert inward-normal inner skin + silhouette-only rim walls = watertight thin slab; interior shared edges get no wall), and detachPanel (extract+solidify+seat a pivot, return {panel, body} with the faces removed from the body so there is no coincident z-fighting skin). Wired into Studio.tsx as a 'detach' button beside glass in face mode (≥1 face), a new onAddPart viewport prop to model.addPart, and STUDIO.shellThicknessMeters (2/16 m). Glass carries onto the inner cap so a window stays see-through both sides. 4 new tests, editMesh suite 71/71 green; full hmsc-int cart bundles clean. Pure TSX/TS so it hot-reloads, no Zig rebuild. Answers the 'how much skeleton is there' question: wheels are the one generated helper, every other panel is now a peeled face-group + joint.
